keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Aeolian (Natural Minor) with Gallop Rhythm & Twin Harmonized Leads

scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G - A - B - C - D
scalesUsed.application: The immortal dual-guitar twin lead harmony moving in parallel diatonic thirds
Dave Murray's fluid legato solo and Adrian Smith's bluesy melodic phrases

scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G - A - B - C# - D
scalesUsed.application: The raised 6th degree (C#) adding brightness during select lead fills

mainProgression.description: The definitive New Wave of British Heavy Metal (NWOBHM) galloping minor cadence

sectionProgressions.description: Twin guitars harmonize the vocal-like lead line in diatonic thirds over Steve Harris' galloping bass
High-speed galloping rhythm rhythmically mimicking charging cavalry horses ('You'll take my life but I'll take yours too')
Triumphant arena refrain sung by tens of thousands of fans worldwide
Adrian Smith's punchy, melodic solo featuring aggressive full-step bends, blues boxes, and biting bridge pickup tone

sectionProgressions.section: Dave Murray Guitar Solo (Fast Legato Cascades)
sectionProgressions.description: Dave Murray's lightning-fast neck-pickup legato hammer-on/pull-off cascades
Climactic return of the twin harmony theme over charging gallops ending on a thunderous low E power chord

harmonicFunction: The natural minor cadence (i - ♭VI - ♭VII - i) creates heroic, battle-hardened gravitas without requiring complex modulations
Harmonizing in diatonic thirds (lower guitar on E minor melody, upper guitar a diatonic third above in G major/E minor) produces rich classical counterpoint
The galloping rhythm (eighth note followed by two sixteenth notes: 'DA-da-da, DA-da-da') provides relentless, breathless drive
Open low E power chord provides a thunderous acoustic floor for twin high-register guitar melodies

techniques.name: Twin-Guitar Diatonic Harmony in 3rds
techniques.description: Playing synchronized dual-guitar lead lines separated by a diatonic third across the high strings

notes: The hallmark sound of Iron Maiden (Dave Murray and Adrian Smith)
Guitar 1 plays root melody: E - F# - G - F# - E - D - E - F#
Guitar 2 plays a diatonic third above: G - A - B - A - G - F# - G - A
Both guitarists must execute matching vibrato and note durations simultaneously
sequence: Position fretting hand in 12th-15th fret box on high E and B strings
Coordinate alternate picking on eighth notes at 160 BPM
Lock into unison vibrato on sustained notes
tips: Practice with a metronome to ensure pick attacks are laser-tight
Record one guitar part and play the harmonized second part on top to verify intonation

techniques.name: High-Speed Iron Maiden Gallop Picking
techniques.description: Executing the signature 'eighth note + two sixteenth notes' gallop picking pattern at 160 BPM

notes: Mimics the rhythmic sound of charging cavalry hooves (DA-da-da, DA-da-da)
Picking pattern: Down, Down-Up (or Down, Up-Down)
Requires tight right-hand palm muting directly over the bridge saddles
tips: Keep the picking wrist light and springy to avoid forearm tension
Accentuate the first note of each triplet group to maintain rhythmic drive

sections.name: Main Harmonized Lead Theme (Smith & Murray)
sections.description: One of the most famous guitar melodies in heavy metal history, harmonized in soaring diatonic thirds.
notes: Synchronized alternate picking at 160 BPM
Execute wide, singing finger vibrato on sustained resolution notes
Let the underlying power chords crash in on the transitions

sections.name: Verse Cavalry Gallop Rhythm
sections.description: The breathless cavalry gallop backing Bruce Dickinson's legendary vocals.
notes: Strict palm-muted gallop picking (eighth + two sixteenths)
Punch the power chord accents on the chord changes
Maintain unrelenting speed and precision

sections.name: Chorus Power Chords & Battle Cries ('Ooh-ooh')
sections.description: Triumphant arena anthem power chords supporting Dickinson's towering battle cries.
notes: Let the heavy power chords ring with maximum arena sustain
Punch the syncopated chord transitions on the offbeat
Prepare for the rapid solo handoffs

sections.name: Adrian Smith Guitar Solo (Blues-Rock Precision)
sections.description: Adrian Smith's punchy, melodic solo featuring aggressive full-step bends, blues boxes, and biting bridge pickup tone.
notes: Smith uses bridge pickup with aggressive full-step bends
Target the root E at fret 12 on the high E string
Precise blues scale phrasing with stinging finger vibrato

sections.name: Dave Murray Guitar Solo (Fast Legato Cascades)
sections.description: Dave Murray's lightning-fast neck-pickup legato hammer-on/pull-off cascades seamlessly picking up from Smith.
notes: Murray switches to neck pickup for fluid, rounded legato runs
Continuous 16th-note hammer-ons and pull-offs in the 12th position
Ascending scale run leading back into the gallop rhythm

sections.name: Outro Harmonized Gallop & Final Hit
sections.description: Climactic return of the twin harmony theme over charging gallops ending on a thunderous low E power chord.
notes: Final dual guitar harmony melody at peak energy
Charging gallop rhythm underneath
Decisive final unison chord hit on beat 1

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster with DiMarzio Super Distortion bridge humbucker (Dave Murray) or Gibson Les Paul (Adrian Smith)
alternatives: Jackson Pro Series Adrian Smith San Dimas

amp.recommended: Marshall JCM800 2203 100W or Marshall 1959 Super Lead with Celestion G12-65s

effects.distortion: Ibanez TS9 Tube Screamer pushing cranked Marshall preamp
effects.reverb: Short stage room reverb with subtle stereo delay (240ms)
effects.other: Dunlop Cry Baby Wah, MXR Phase 90

beginner.title: Em-C-D Progression & Basic Harmony Melody
steps: Learn the i - ♭VI - ♭VII power chord progression (Em5, C5, D5)
Memorize the single-guitar intro melody at 100 BPM
Practice smooth chord transitions without dropping tempo

intermediate.title: Gallop Picking Rhythm Mechanics
steps: Master the eighth + two sixteenths gallop picking pattern
Build right-hand wrist stamina up to 160 BPM
Learn the upper-register harmonized 3rd melody part

advanced.title: Dual Guitar Solos & Tight Twin Lead Locking
steps: Learn Adrian Smith's bluesy lead solo with aggressive bends and vibrato
Master Dave Murray's fluid neck-pickup legato hammer-on/pull-off runs
Perform with a partner or second track with exact unison pitch and timing

commonMistakes: Playing straight sixteenth notes instead of the galloping 'eighth + two sixteenths' rhythm
Rushing the tempo during the fast twin-guitar harmony intro
Muting notes poorly during the fast legato runs, causing dissonant string bleed
practiceRoutine: 5 min: Alternate picking and gallop rhythm warm-up at 120 BPM
10 min: Main harmony theme accuracy drills at 130 BPM with metronome
15 min: Solo study: isolating Smith's bends and Murray's legato phrases
10 min: Full gallop endurance run-through at 160 BPM
focusAreas: Laser-sharp twin lead intonation and unison vibrato
Relaxed, fatigue-free gallop picking wrist mechanics
Dynamic separation between heavy rhythm gallops and soaring leads
metronomeWork: Practice gallop picking starting at 120 BPM with sixteenth-note clicks
Bump tempo by 5 BPM daily until reaching 160 BPM
Focus on accenting the first note of each gallop grouping
